entries.test: Public deployment records and interpretability research can establish whether AI development was advancing despite substantial gaps in understanding system behavior in October 2023.
entries.note: The skiing metaphor accompanies a substantive claim about development and understanding.
Neither 'all that close' nor intelligence exceeding humans has a shared threshold here.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations of October 2023 generative AI on genuinely novel inference problems can test whether it reliably reasons adaptively and flexibly.
entries.note: Marcus supplies a behavioral interpretation of intelligence and understanding through novel reasoning and concrete failures.
The conclusion concerns whether we should attribute deep understanding.

entries.test: Public studies comparing generative AI performance on familiar patterns and novel variations can test whether much of its performance consists of unreliable imitation.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give mimicry a concrete reading involving familiar patterns and failed generalization.
Rejecting an asserted equivalence as a 'bridge too far' is weaker than categorically denying it. The sense of experience at issue also lacks an agreed test.
No shared definition or decisive public test of machine consciousness is specified.

entries.test: Public reliability evaluations, factuality tests, and descriptions of factual grounding methods can test these assertions about contemporary AI systems.
entries.note: The normalization broadens criticism centered on generative AI to neural network AI systems generally.

entries.test: Representative surveys or recorded forecasts of expected generative AI capabilities, compared with demonstrated capabilities by October 2023, could establish whether most people's expectations were exceeded.
entries.note: Measuring past expectations is difficult but does not inherently preclude public evidence.
Calling a declaration of victory premature evaluates whether the evidence warrants that declaration.

Marcus objects to comparing connection counts 'in this way'; the normalization rejects direct comparisons generally. Its conclusion is a methodological judgment, although the biological differences are factual.

entries.test: Public factual accuracy and consistency evaluations of contemporary chatbots can establish whether their information frequently contains gaps and errors.
entries.note: Marcus deliberately says 'information' and 'whatever’s there' while disputing its equivalence to human knowledge.

entries.test: Public debugging studies, predictability evaluations, and factual grounding demonstrations can test whether limited mechanistic understanding causes these engineering limitations.
entries.note: Nobody knowing how to guarantee grounding does not establish impossibility. 'Unpredictable' also strengthens 'difficult to predict'.

entries.test: Public engineering case studies and company accounts of adoption decisions can establish whether AI unpredictability creates substantial engineering difficulty and contributes to cautious adoption.
entries.note: Publicly documented company decisions can support this claim without requiring access to private motives.

entries.test: Published guarantees and counterexamples involving contemporary AI hallucinations and generated code can establish whether reliable general guarantees against those errors existed.
entries.note: Read in context, this concerns available guarantees for current systems.
'Way too much authority' judges the acceptable balance of authority and control.

entries.test: Documented cases of machines manipulating people before publication and a substantial accumulation of additional cases afterward would establish the asserted pattern.
entries.note: The historical component is checkable now; the future increase has no deadline.
This is a legislative recommendation.

entries.test: Comparisons of Bard's output with preexisting stories, together with public evidence of reproduction and infringement across LLM outputs, can test the copying and characteristic infringement claims.
entries.note: The existence of the famous prompt alone would not establish copying or intellectual property infringement.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of strong next-word prediction by systems that fail corresponding comprehension and inference tasks can test whether prediction performance necessarily establishes understanding.
entries.note: The surrounding passage supplies a concrete lookup-based counterexample and behavioral interpretation.

entries.test: Public evaluations of contemporary LLM fact-checking capabilities and repeated reasoning errors can test the factual grounds Marcus gives for denying intelligence.
entries.note: The categorical incapacity to fact-check is independently falsifiable; intelligence is interpreted through his stated behavioral criteria.

entries.test: Public employment and deployment records showing any radiologist replaced by a machine between 2016 and October 10, 2023 would refute the zero-replacement claim.
entries.note: The question is immediately answered with an asserted number, so this is not merely rhetoric.

entries.test: Comparative medical imaging studies available by October 2023 can establish whether combined human and AI assessment outperformed either alone.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion fixes the domain as radiology.

entries.test: Public evaluations comparing contemporary AI and radiologists on image interpretation and integrated clinical cases can test the claimed differences in capability.
entries.note: Case files and notes make 'big picture' sufficiently concrete to test.

entries.test: Public clinical trial results and regulatory records as of October 10, 2023 can establish whether any AI-designed drug had demonstrated therapeutic efficacy.
entries.note: The normalization omits 'as far as I know'; listing it separately does not preserve the hedge in the proposition.

entries.test: Public evidence of substantial changes in drug discovery productivity, development practice, or successful drugs attributable to AI would establish a big impact on drug design.
entries.note: The impact prediction is firm; uncertainty concerns which techniques will deliver it.

entries.test: Public investigations documenting large-scale automated AI fake-news operations aimed at manipulating both markets and elections would establish the firm forecast.
entries.note: The normalization omits 'wholesale,' weakening the scale requirement. The separate possibility of undermining democracy is not independently settleable.

entries.test: Public incident investigations and comparative safety evaluations can test whether accelerated AI development and deployment increase risk.
entries.note: The normalization turns Marcus's inability to see a guarantee into a broader assertion that no path is visible. The causal risk claim is independently testable.
Greater personal worry does not assert a greater objective risk. The remaining takeover claim only says the possibility cannot be ruled out.
Making the 'right choices' is a normative appeal; the turning-point language supplies no independent agreed test.
